newsitem.title: CANADA: British Columbia gives details on budget, job cuts.
newsitem.headline: British Columbia gives details on budget, job cuts.

text.p: British Columbia Finance Minister Andrew Petter outlined Thursday C$437 million in budget cuts and elimination of 2,334 civil service jobs.
The cuts are spread over the next 18 months with C$169 million and 444 of the job cuts due before the end of the current fiscal year in March.
The cuts are part of a program announced in September to save C$750 million over 18 months. They also detail the elimination of 3,500 government jobs announced by Premier Glen Clark on Tuesday.
Petter said the cuts include one-time only savings as well as continuing overhead reductions from a smaller payroll and closure of offices.

Thursday's announcement covered cuts to 12 of 16 government ministries. Cuts in the others will be announced next week. Hardest hit in Thursday's round were the education ministry which will lose 192 jobs; the environment ministry which will lose 285 and the forests ministry which will lose 525 jobs.
Petter said 2,500 workers will be offered early retirement at a cost of C$20 million to C$50 million.
Petter said that cost could be absorbed by the provincial pension fund which has a surplus.

Petter declined to comment on the possibility of a revision to the government's debt reduction plan. Premier Glen Clark told the Vancouver Sun that the plan is under review and may be revised. The plan was introduced two years ago and aims to reduce the province's direct debt by C$1.3 billion by 2000.
